elong_meso_component_escape_alignment → elong_micro_component_projection downward When the component major axis is escape-aligned, fish positions along that axis are reshaped, plausibly changing individual normalized projections onto the component axis.

elong_meso_component_escape_alignment → wave_micro_escape_alignment downward A component whose elongation aligns with mean escape direction provides a directional context that can bias individual fish headings toward their own escape directions.

elong_meso_component_escape_alignment → pol_micro_neighbor_alignment downward Component-level elongation and escape alignment alter the spatial arrangement of neighbors, plausibly changing the heading alignment a focal fish experiences locally.

elong_meso_component_escape_alignment → comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance downward An escape-aligned stretched component changes nearest-neighbor geometry, plausibly increasing or decreasing a focal fish's nearest contact distance.

fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction → wave_micro_heading_change downward When many component contacts involve frightened fish, local escape turns become more likely, plausibly increasing individual heading-change magnitude.

fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction → fright_micro_state downward A high fraction of frightened contact edges in a component increases social fright exposure, making a focal fish's transition into fright more likely.

fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction → fright_micro_remaining downward Dense frightened-edge contexts can prolong or reset local fright pressure, plausibly affecting the remaining fright duration of a focal fish.

fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction → pol_micro_heading_deviation downward A frightened-edge-rich component can locally disorder headings through escape responses, plausibly raising focal deviation from the school mean heading.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → pol_micro_neighbor_alignment downward More contacts in a component increase social heading input, plausibly strengthening a focal fish's alignment with contact neighbors.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → comp_micro_degree downward A component with higher mean degree offers more potential contact partners, plausibly raising the realized contact degree of a focal fish in that component.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance downward Higher component connectivity can bring neighbors closer or create crowding, plausibly changing a focal fish's nearest contact distance.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → comp_micro_clustering_coefficient downward Component-level contact density can create more neighbor-of-neighbor links, plausibly increasing a focal fish's local clustering coefficient.

lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction → wave_micro_heading_change downward Frequent cascade-matched turns within a component can increase individual step heading changes as followers adjust to leaders.
lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction → pol_micro_neighbor_alignment downward Cascading turns tend to align neighbors, plausibly raising a focal fish's heading alignment with contact neighbors.

lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction → lead_micro_lagged_alignment downward A component with many sign-matched cascades provides a stronger lagged turning context, plausibly increasing focal alignment with previous neighbor heading changes.

lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction → lead_micro_influence_score downward Cascade-rich components can amplify some individuals' turns, plausibly raising the run-level lagged influence score of a focal fish.

frag_macro_component_count → frag_micro_isolate downward Fragmentation can leave marginal fish outside dense subgroups, making individual contact isolation more likely through changed local neighbor availability.

frag_macro_component_count → pol_micro_neighbor_alignment downward More components imply fewer cross-group neighbors for a fish, which can change the local heading reference and reduce alignment with contact neighbors.
frag_macro_component_count → comp_micro_degree downward A more fragmented group context alters how many neighbors a focal fish can maintain, plausibly lowering its realized contact degree.

frag_macro_component_count → frag_meso_mean_component_size downward More contact components change the local grouping context in which fish merge or split, plausibly lowering the average component size observed at the meso level.

frag_macro_component_count → frag_meso_component_size_entropy downward A higher number of components can redistribute fish among subgroups, plausibly raising the entropy of component sizes through repeated splitting and partial re-merging.

frag_macro_component_count → comp_meso_component_mean_degree downward When the school is split into more components, fish interactions become confined to smaller subsets, plausibly reducing the mean contact degree within components.

frag_macro_largest_fraction → frag_meso_mean_component_size downward When the largest connected fraction grows or shrinks through merging and splitting, the remaining small components are redistributed, so the mean component size can shift dynamically rather than being a fixed identity.

frag_macro_largest_fraction → elong_meso_component_axis_length downward A dominant largest component can absorb or shed peripheral groups; this changes which fish belong to a component and therefore alters that component's spatial spread along its major axis.

frag_macro_largest_fraction → wave_meso_component_escape_coherence downward The global share of fish in one component controls how many escape-direction biases are mixed inside components, so component-level escape coherence can be diluted or reinforced by global fragmentation.

frag_macro_largest_fraction → fright_meso_component_fright_position_corr downward When most fish belong to one connected component, fright states and positions are mixed over a larger set; when fragmentation isolates groups, frightened individuals are spatially sorted differently within components.

frag_macro_largest_fraction → pol_meso_component_polarization downward Merging into a dominant component can combine sub-groups with different headings, changing component polarization; splitting can preserve locally aligned sub-groups instead.

frag_macro_largest_fraction → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance downward Global connectivity changes which fish are counted together in a component and can bring distant sub-groups into the same component, shifting the mean nearest-contact spacing inside components.

frag_macro_largest_fraction → mill_meso_component_angular_velocity downward A larger dominant component can sustain shear across more fish, while fragmented small components rotate around local centroids, so global largest-fraction changes can alter component angular velocity.

frag_macro_largest_fraction → lead_meso_component_influence_variance downward Global fragmentation changes which fish share a component and therefore how heterogeneous leader/follower influence scores are within components.

frag_macro_component_count_change → frag_meso_component_size_entropy downward Stepwise splitting or merging of contact components redistributes fish among component sizes, so a macro change in component count can alter the meso entropy of component sizes through the same fragmentation dynamics.

frag_macro_component_count_change → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation downward When the school breaks into more components, fish that remain grouped may be exposed to different local social cues, changing within-component heading scatter and thus the meso mean deviation.

frag_macro_component_count_change → mill_meso_component_rotational_order downward Fragmentation interrupts coherent circulation by separating fish into smaller groups, which can reduce the tendency for component-level tangential directions to align into rotational order.

elong_macro_school_aspect_ratio → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment downward A whole-school elongation axis shapes the geometry in which component fish turn and flee, so components stretched along that axis tend to have headings more aligned with their escape directions.

elong_macro_school_aspect_ratio → mill_meso_component_rotational_order downward Strong whole-school elongation opposes circular geometry by stretching positions and velocities along one direction, which can suppress the tangential alignment needed for component rotational order.

elong_macro_anisotropy_index → frag_meso_centroid_pair_distance downward When the school is globally elongated, components may be pushed apart along the major axis, increasing distances between component centroids.

elong_macro_anisotropy_index → elong_meso_component_aspect_ratio downward Higher whole-school anisotropy implies global stretching along a major axis, imposing a shared strain field that locally elongates contact components and increases their aspect ratio.

elong_macro_anisotropy_index → pol_meso_component_away_shark_alignment downward Global anisotropy aligned with escape direction may reinforce local component alignment away from the shark, as components inherit the global directional bias.

elong_macro_anisotropy_index → mill_meso_component_angular_momentum downward Global elongation may suppress rotational milling by imposing a linear escape direction, reducing component angular momentum.

elong_macro_major_escape_alignment → elong_micro_major_projection downward When the school major axis is escape-aligned, individual projections onto that axis are reorganized by the collective stretching, plausibly shifting focal normalized projections.

elong_macro_major_escape_alignment → wave_micro_escape_alignment downward Whole-school alignment of elongation with escape direction provides a directional field that can make individual heading-escape alignment more likely.

elong_macro_major_escape_alignment → elong_meso_component_escape_alignment downward Whole-school major-axis escape alignment creates a global directional axis that can propagate into component-level elongation and escape alignment.

elong_macro_major_escape_alignment → wave_meso_component_escape_coherence downward A school-level escape-aligned elongation can synchronize component escape directions, plausibly raising coherence within contact components.

elong_macro_major_escape_alignment → pol_meso_component_polarization downward Global elongation along a common escape axis can bias component headings toward that axis, plausibly increasing component polarization.

wave_macro_school_escape_coherence → wave_micro_escape_alignment downward School-level escape coherence acts as a shared directional context that can increase individual heading alignment with own escape direction.
wave_macro_school_escape_coherence → wave_micro_heading_change downward As a coherent escape wave passes, individual fish are plausibly induced to turn, changing step heading-change magnitudes.

wave_macro_school_escape_coherence → pol_micro_neighbor_alignment downward A school-wide coherent escape direction can make neighboring headings more similar, plausibly raising focal alignment with contact neighbors.

wave_macro_school_escape_coherence → wave_meso_component_escape_coherence downward High school-wide escape-direction coherence provides a common directional drive that can increase coherence within contact components.

wave_macro_school_escape_coherence → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment downward A coherent school escape wave can align component fish headings with their escape directions, plausibly raising component mean alignment.

wave_macro_heading_change_shark_cov → frag_meso_mean_component_size downward Heterogeneous turning near versus far from sharks can shear contact neighborhoods, merging or breaking components and thereby changing mean component size.

wave_macro_heading_change_shark_cov → elong_meso_component_axis_length downward When heading changes are strongly coupled to shark proximity, fish near the shark turn away and stretch local components along the escape direction, increasing component major-axis length.

wave_macro_heading_change_shark_cov → wave_meso_component_escape_coherence downward A strong global covariance between turning and proximity implies coordinated threat response; this can align escape directions inside components and raise component escape coherence.

wave_macro_heading_change_shark_cov → fright_meso_component_fright_position_corr downward Differential turning by shark proximity redistributes frightened and non-frightened fish within components, altering the correlation between fright state and distance from component centroid.

wave_macro_heading_change_shark_cov → pol_meso_component_polarization downward If heading changes are globally tuned to shark proximity, nearby fish turn similarly while distant fish turn less, which can either sharpen or break component-level heading alignment.

wave_macro_heading_change_shark_cov → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance downward Turning responses that depend on shark distance change local crowding: fish near a shark may compress or spread, which shifts mean nearest-contact distance within components.

wave_macro_heading_change_shark_cov → mill_meso_component_angular_velocity downward A proximity-dependent turning field can impose tangential motion on one side of a component and weaker motion on the other, generating or suppressing component angular velocity.

wave_macro_heading_change_shark_cov → lead_meso_component_influence_variance downward Heterogeneous threat-driven turns make some fish lead and others follow, so the global heading-change/proximity covariance can be associated with variance in component influence scores.

wave_macro_escape_coherence_change → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment downward A rising school-wide escape-direction coherence propagates into contact components, making component fish more likely to share a common escape heading and raising component mean heading-escape alignment.

wave_macro_escape_coherence_change → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation downward A coherent escape wave tends to sweep local heading adjustments through components, reducing the scatter of component headings around their mean during the wave passage.

fright_macro_school_prevalence → frag_meso_component_size_entropy downward Widespread fright increases local avoidance and escape motion, which can break contact links unevenly and thereby reshape the distribution of component sizes toward smaller or more varied components.

fright_macro_school_prevalence → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment downward High school fright prevalence supplies many fish with active escape directions, so component members are more likely to align their headings with those escape directions.

fright_macro_school_fright_edge_fraction → wave_meso_component_turn_variance downward Widespread fright edges may increase local turn variability as fish react individually, raising component turn variance.

fright_macro_school_fright_edge_fraction → fright_meso_component_prevalence downward A high global fraction of frightened edges indicates widespread fright contagion, which can raise the local prevalence of frightened fish within components through increased exposure.

fright_macro_school_fright_edge_fraction → pol_meso_component_away_shark_alignment downward Widespread fright at the global edge level can drive local components to orient away from the shark, as frightened fish collectively bias component headings.

fright_macro_school_fright_edge_fraction → comp_meso_component_edge_density downward High global frightened-edge fraction may cause fish to aggregate more tightly, altering local component edge density; we posit increased clustering of frightened fish raises density.
fright_macro_onset_rate → wave_micro_heading_change downward Fright onset events are accompanied by escape turns, so school-wide onset rate can plausibly increase individual step heading changes.
fright_macro_onset_rate → fright_micro_state downward A higher school-level onset rate increases local contagion pressure, making an individual fish's fright state more probable.

fright_macro_onset_rate → fright_meso_component_prevalence downward Higher school-wide fright onset introduces new frightened fish into local components, plausibly raising component fright prevalence.

fright_macro_onset_rate → fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction downward A rising onset rate increases the chance that both endpoints of a local contact become frightened, plausibly raising frightened-edge fractions.
fright_macro_onset_rate → pol_meso_component_polarization downward Widespread fright onset can trigger coordinated escape turns within components, plausibly increasing component heading polarization.

pol_macro_school_polarization → wave_micro_escape_alignment downward High whole-school polarization can align individual headings with the prevailing escape direction, plausibly raising heading-escape alignment.
pol_macro_school_polarization → pol_micro_heading_deviation downward A polarized collective heading can constrain individual headings, plausibly reducing focal deviation from the school mean.

pol_macro_school_polarization → pol_micro_neighbor_alignment downward School-level polarization implies more similar headings across neighbors, plausibly increasing a focal fish's alignment with its contact neighbors.
pol_macro_school_polarization → pol_meso_component_polarization downward A highly polarized school provides a strong common heading field that can raise polarization within contact components.

pol_macro_school_polarization → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation downward When school-wide polarization is high, component headings are plausibly drawn toward the common direction, reducing mean component heading deviation.

pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → frag_meso_mean_component_size downward A run-level regime in which polarization tracks shark proximity can make fish align and move together under threat, changing how contact components merge or split.

pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → elong_meso_component_axis_length downward When global polarization is coupled to proximity, threat-aligned motion can stretch components along the shared heading, increasing their major-axis length.

pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → wave_meso_component_escape_coherence downward Global polarization-proximity coupling indicates how strongly threat proximity aligns headings; this conditions whether escape directions within components are coherent.

pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → fright_meso_component_fright_position_corr downward If polarization and proximity covary, frightened fish may be concentrated near threat-facing edges of components, changing the within-component fright-position correlation.

pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → pol_meso_component_polarization downward The run-level polarization-proximity coupling sets how much local components align during threat, so component-level polarization can vary with this global coupling regime.

pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance downward Threat-coupled alignment changes how fish pack while moving together; stronger coupling can compress or loosen nearest-neighbor spacing inside components.

pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → mill_meso_component_angular_velocity downward If global polarization rises near sharks, components may favor straight escape over rotation; weak coupling may allow vortex-like local motion, altering component angular velocity.

pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov → lead_meso_component_influence_variance downward Threat-coupled polarization can make some individuals' turns dominate others, changing within-component heterogeneity of leader/follower influence.

pol_macro_polarization_change → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation downward An increase in whole-school heading polarization reflects stronger collective alignment, which can propagate into components and reduce the mean angular deviation of component headings.

comp_macro_school_mean_degree → frag_meso_component_size_entropy downward Higher whole-school contact degree means denser local connectivity, which tends to merge contact components and reduce the meso entropy of component sizes.
comp_macro_school_clustering → frag_meso_centroid_pair_distance downward Strong global clustering may make components more compact and closer together, reducing centroid pair distances.

comp_macro_school_clustering → comp_meso_component_edge_density downward Higher global clustering coefficient reflects a more tightly knit contact network, which can locally densify components, raising their edge density.
comp_macro_school_clustering → mill_meso_component_angular_momentum downward Strong global clustering may promote coherent rotational motion within dense components, increasing angular momentum.
comp_macro_school_clustering → lead_meso_component_lagged_alignment downward Dense global clustering facilitates local propagation of heading changes, enhancing lagged alignment within components.

comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance → frag_micro_isolate downward Larger school-wide nearest-contact spacing makes it more likely that a marginal fish has no recorded contact neighbor, increasing isolation.
comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance → comp_micro_degree downward When the school is more spread out, individual fish have fewer close contacts, plausibly reducing focal contact degree.

comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance → comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance downward School-level spacing sets the local crowding regime, plausibly shifting the nearest contact distance experienced by an individual fish.

comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance → comp_meso_component_edge_density downward Larger typical nearest-neighbor spacing reduces the chance of local contacts, plausibly lowering component edge density.

comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance downward A school-wide increase in nearest-contact spacing can propagate into component geometry, plausibly raising mean nearest-contact distance within components.

mill_macro_school_angular_velocity → mill_micro_angular_velocity downward A school-level angular velocity can bias individual tangential motion around the collective center, plausibly changing focal angular velocity.

mill_macro_school_angular_velocity → mill_micro_tangential_speed downward Global milling supplies a shared tangential direction, plausibly increasing or decreasing a focal fish's signed tangential speed.

mill_macro_school_angular_velocity → mill_micro_radial_velocity downward Rotational collective motion can balance inward social attraction and outward escape, plausibly altering individual radial velocity.

mill_macro_school_angular_velocity → mill_meso_component_angular_velocity downward A global rotational tendency provides a kinematic context that can induce component-level angular velocity through shared turning and neighbor coupling.

mill_macro_school_angular_velocity → mill_meso_component_rotational_order downward Whole-school milling can organize local tangential motions, plausibly increasing rotational order within contact components.

mill_macro_school_rotational_order → frag_meso_mean_component_size downward A globally rotating school imposes tangential shear that can tear and re-form contact components, changing mean component size.

mill_macro_school_rotational_order → elong_meso_component_axis_length downward Global rotational order stretches components along the tangential direction while compressing them radially, which can change component major-axis length.

mill_macro_school_rotational_order → wave_meso_component_escape_coherence downward Strong global rotation competes with unified escape headings, so component escape-direction coherence may be reduced when rotational order is high.

mill_macro_school_rotational_order → fright_meso_component_fright_position_corr downward Rotational motion redistributes fish around component centroids, so frightened individuals become spatially arranged by orbit rather than by simple outward distance, changing the fright-position correlation.

mill_macro_school_rotational_order → pol_meso_component_polarization downward Global rotational order implies headings are organized tangentially, which can lower component heading polarization by canceling opposing headings on opposite sides.

mill_macro_school_rotational_order → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance downward Rotation changes local crowding through centrifugal spreading and tangential shear, shifting nearest-contact distances within components.

mill_macro_school_rotational_order → mill_meso_component_angular_velocity downward A globally rotating school can entrain component-scale vortices; component angular velocity should be responsive to the presence and sign of school-level rotational order.

mill_macro_school_rotational_order → lead_meso_component_influence_variance downward When the whole school rotates coherently, many fish share the same turning tendency, which can reduce the distinction between leaders and followers inside components.

mill_macro_school_angular_momentum → mill_meso_component_rotational_order downward A whole-school rotational bias provides a common tangential drive that can organize component fish into aligned tangential motion, increasing component rotational order.
lead_macro_school_cascade_fraction → wave_meso_component_turn_variance downward Global cascades may synchronize turns, reducing variance in requested turns within components.
lead_macro_school_cascade_fraction → pol_meso_component_away_shark_alignment downward Global cascade alignment may bias component headings away from the shark, increasing away-shark alignment.

lead_macro_school_cascade_fraction → lead_meso_component_lagged_alignment downward A high global cascade fraction indicates widespread sign-matched heading changes, which can amplify local lagged alignment within components.

lead_macro_school_influence_variance → lead_micro_lagged_alignment downward When influence is highly variable school-wide, a focal fish's current turn is plausibly more or less aligned with earlier neighbor turns depending on its local leaders.

lead_macro_school_influence_variance → lead_micro_influence_score downward A wide school-level influence distribution implies that a focal fish's lagged influence score is shaped by uneven leader-follower dynamics.

lead_macro_school_influence_variance → lead_meso_component_lagged_alignment downward High variance in influence scores creates uneven leader-follower roles, plausibly altering component mean lagged heading-change alignment.

lead_macro_school_influence_variance → lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction downward A school-wide spread of influential individuals can produce more sign-matched turning sequences, plausibly raising component cascade fraction.

lead_macro_school_influence_variance → lead_meso_component_influence_variance downward Global heterogeneity in influence scores can concentrate or disperse leadership within components, plausibly changing component influence variance.

N1 | frag_micro_component_size Contact-component size of focal fish Scale: micro | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: For run r and step t, let G_t=(V_t,E_t) be the undirected graph with fish nodes V_t from agent_states role='fish' and edges E_t from contacts pairs {agent_id,partner_id} at (r,t). For focal fish i in V_t, let C_t(i) be its connected component in G_t. Indicator = |C_t(i)|. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N2 | frag_micro_isolate Focal fish contact isolation flag Scale: micro | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: For fish i at (r,t), let k_i(t)=|{j: (i,j) in E_t or (j,i) in E_t}|. Indicator = 1 if k_i(t)=0, else 0. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N3 | frag_micro_component_shark_distance Focal component centroid to nearest shark distance Scale: micro | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: Let c_C(t)=mean_{j in C_t(i)} p_j(t) for focal fish i. Let D_i(t)=min_{s in sharks at t} ||c_C(t)-p_s(t)||. Indicator = D_i(t). Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N10 | elong_micro_major_projection Focal fish normalized major-axis projection Scale: micro | Phenomenon: school_elongation Definition: Let c=mean_i p_i and C=(1/N) sum_i (p_i-c)(p_i-c)^T for all fish at (r,t). Let lambda1>=lambda2 be eigenvalues and u1 the unit eigenvector for lambda1. For fish i, indicator=(p_i-c)·u1/sqrt(lambda1).
